mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate is persistently below its long-run average for at least 3 consecutive months, market expectations of future rate hikes diminish, lowering discount rates and boosting equity present-value pricing, which drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < mean(FEDFUNDS) over the past 12 months for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not statistically higher than the 12-month pre-signal baseline (t-test p > 0.05) during qualifying low-rate periods.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) coinciding with a decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strengthening labor market, prompting optimism about corporate hiring and productivity, which elevates S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by at least 2% month-over-month AND UNRATE falls by at least 0.2 percentage points in the same month
failure_condition: During qualifying labor-market turning events, SPX 20-day forward returns are negative or flat, and the joint index correlation (PAYEMS*UNRATE) is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly rise in consumer demand proxies (HOUST) accompanied by a decline in industrial production (INDPRO) indicates a shift from supply-side to demand-side growth, which boosts equity valuations via expectations of stronger earnings and profit margins over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases by ≥ 3% month-over-month AND INDPRO decreases by ≥ 2% month-over-month for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are not statistically positive relative to the prior 30-day average (t-test p > 0.05) during such transitions.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) followed by a sustained drop in consumer inflation (CPIAUCSL) suggests supply-side constraints are easing, allowing for faster price adjustment and higher real earnings growth, which supports positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by ≥ 4% month-over-month AND CPIAUCSL falls by ≥ 0.5% month-over-month for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: During supply-chain easing episodes, SPX 20-day forward returns are flat or negative, and the interaction term (INDPRO*CPIAUCSL) shows no predictive power (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) crosses above 4% for the first time in a tightening cycle, accompanied by a rise in inflation (CPIAUCSL), markets anticipate a near-term policy pause, elevating risk premiums and compressing discount rates, which tends to produce negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE crosses above 4% AND CPIAUCSL increases by ≥ 0.2% in the same month
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than the prior 60-day average during such policy onset events (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A prolonged period of declining labor participation (PAYEMS) without a corresponding decline in unemployment (UNRATE) suggests demographic or confidence-driven weak demand, which can depress corporate earnings expectations and produce negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS decreases by ≥ 2% month-over-month for 3 consecutive months AND UNRATE remains below 5% during the same window
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than the prior 60-day average during such participation declines (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden spike in retail sales (HOUST) without a corresponding rise in industrial production (INDPRO) indicates demand-side excess, which can overheat the economy and prompt a sharp equity correction; this mechanism predicts negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases by ≥ 8% month-over-month AND INDPRO remains flat or increases by < 1% in the same month
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are not statistically negative relative to the prior 30-day average during such spikes (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A rapid deceleration in consumer inflation (CPIAUCSL) while industrial production remains flat or declines suggests supply-side rigidity, raising uncertainty about future output and pushing down equity valuations; this mechanism predicts negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL falls by ≥ 0.7% month-over-month AND INDPRO does not increase by ≥ 1% in the same month
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not statistically negative during such episodes (p > 0.05).
